RQ1.rationale: Central paper on general CubeSat reference model/logical architecture adaptable to any CubeSat project.

RQ2.rationale: Claims outcomes around reuse, consistency, burden reduction, integration, and decision support, but evidence is weak and not EPS-specific.

RQ3.rationale: Mentions V&V strategies/testing requirements and MBSE V&V support, but no EPS verification procedure model is presented.

bibliographic_review_management.lineage_overlap_notes: Part of INCOSE SSWG MBSE Challenge CubeSat reference-model lineage. Paper summarizes phases 1-3 including RAX, behavior modeling/power-comm-state, enterprise model, and trade studies, and identifies current phase 4. Related earlier/later papers include references [4], [6], [10]-[13], [17]. Avoid double-counting RAX simulations/trade-study outcomes across lineage papers.

mbse_objective_scope_artifacts.stated_objective_pain_point: Provide a sufficiently complete CubeSat Reference Model/guide/tool for teams, especially first-time low-budget CubeSat groups, and demonstrate MBSE/OOSEM for CubeSat missions including concept life-cycle trade studies.
mbse_objective_scope_artifacts.system_boundary_and_abstraction: Generic CubeSat mission enterprise and logical architecture, including space system, ground system, launch services, launch vehicle interface system, and communication services. Logical subsystems are provided as abstractions/building blocks; users add/remove subsystems and create mission-specific/physical architecture based on mission requirements and objectives.
mbse_objective_scope_artifacts.minimal_behavioral_or_domain_knowledge_h: The reference model is intended to help teams with limited systems-engineering experience by providing stakeholder categories, standard nomenclature, Cal Poly specification requirements, logical subsystems, and reusable elements. The current phase focuses on logical architecture rather than requiring detailed behavior; prior behavior and constraint equation simulations are summarized from earlier phases.

artifact_details.requirements: Cal Poly CubeSat Design Specification modeled in SysML, including general requirements table with text and Refined By column.
artifact_details.structure_architecture: SysML BDDs for stakeholders, regulatory agencies, mission enterprise, logical ground system, and logical space subsystems.
artifact_details.behavior_parametrics: Behavior diagrams and parametrics are described as SysML views; earlier phases executed system behavior simulations and constraint equations.
artifact_details.trade_studies: MOE/MOP/TPM decomposition and model-parameter identification for concept trade studies; prior RAX trades for energy and data download.
artifact_details.interfaces: Mission enterprise includes launch vehicle interface and communication services; mission-specific model can interface with COTS modeling/simulation tools.

implementation_pathway_tailoring.mapping_to_systems_engineering_activitie: OOSEM maps to analyzing stakeholder needs, analyzing system requirements, defining logical architecture, and synthesizing candidate physical architectures. The paper supports concept life-cycle trade studies and generic V&V/mission-assurance strategy links but does not map to explicit SRR/PDR/CDR gates.
implementation_pathway_tailoring.tailoring_notes: Method is tailored to small, low-cost, short-life-cycle CubeSat teams that may lack full-time systems engineering. Guidance is high-level and artifact-oriented rather than a complete playbook.

toolchain_interoperability_lifecycle_con.toolchain_architecture_data_flow: SysML system model is the core repository; mission-specific model receives requirements, trade studies, mission-specific stakeholders/use cases/viewpoints, CubeSat reference elements, V&V strategies, mission-assurance objectives, COTS modeling/simulation interfaces, and space/ground component library elements. Distribution options include MagicDraw, ZIP file, XMI file, OpenMBEE, and Teamcenter with user feedback to SSWG.
toolchain_interoperability_lifecycle_con.interoperability_details: The paper names XMI and ZIP file distribution and COTS simulation interfaces but does not report API/plugin/co-simulation details, semantic mapping, or automated synchronization.
toolchain_interoperability_lifecycle_con.syntax_semantic_lifecycle_continuity: Conceptual continuity is claimed via the SysML repository containing requirements/design and views that update from model changes; lifecycle scope is conception through retirement in the figure, but detailed downstream continuity is not demonstrated.
toolchain_interoperability_lifecycle_con.software_hardware_system_integration_rea: Not demonstrated. The reference model contains logical architecture, launch/integration stakeholders, and Cal Poly testing/electrical requirements, but no hardware/software integration workflow or testbed linkage.
toolchain_interoperability_lifecycle_con.availability_reproducibility: Distribution process and license are under development; planned distribution mechanisms are named, but the current reference model is not shown as externally available in this paper.

RQ1: Strongly relevant system-level contribution: a SysML/OOSEM CubeSat Reference Model intended as a logical architecture and reusable starting point for any CubeSat mission.

General modeling emphasizes stakeholders, needs/objectives/constraints/MOEs, Cal Poly specification requirements, mission enterprise decomposition, logical space/ground subsystems, and concept trade studies.
The model addresses limited team SE experience by acting as a guide/checklist, but detailed mission-specific validation remains future work.
RQ2: Claims relevant to reproducibility/integrability include reusable reference model, single integrated repository, COTS simulation interfaces, and distribution mechanisms.

Power-related decision-support examples include energy, available power, solar-panel area, battery capacity, data download, and SNR trade studies, but these are not EPS reliability outcomes and lack MBSE-benefit baselines.
Evidence is mostly weak to moderate: conceptual argument and prior RAX simulation/trade demonstrations without quantitative comparison.
RQ3: The paper does not present an EPS verification procedure model prior to physical development.
Generic V&V strategies and Cal Poly testing requirements are mentioned, but verification matrices, test cases/procedures, executable checks, SIL/HIL, or automated tests are not reported.

author_limitations_gaps: Distribution/licensing process still being developed; model must reach minimum structure before external distribution.
Next step is mission-specific example and MOE/MOP validation.
Current effort to date focused on nomenclature/definitions, stakeholders/MOEs, and generic logical architecture.
extractor_identified_limitations_gaps: No quantitative MBSE benefit evaluation or baseline comparator.

Recurring INCOSE SSWG/RAX lineage creates overlap risk for synthesis.
